Administrator of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Lee Zeldin and U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. announced the EPA will now consider microplastics a “priority contaminant group” in the Contaminant Candidate List (CCL6) while HHS will launch a $144 million project to investigate the impact of microplastics on human health. STOMP (Systematic Targeting Of MicroPlastics): HHS division ARPA-H is launching a 5-year program that aims to develop strategies to remove microplastics from people’s bodies.

The 5 Gyres Institute presented the global trend of plastic fragmentation from macro to micro, with 170 trillion particles of microplastics in the world's oceans today. But its the continued fragmentation from micro to nanoplastics that allows the smallest particles of plastics to infiltrate human tissues and organs, documented in our brains, hearts and other organs, with deleterious effects.

This 144 million infusion of funding will go a long way to help researchers measure, monitor and mitigate nanoplastics in the human body.

A study now fuses data from traffic cameras and mobile phones to estimate citywide emissions in near-real time, finding strong spatiotemporal variation and a 16–22% emission drop after congestion pricing.
